question: Rupesh got an increase of 4% in his sales amount in the first year and 25% in the second year; also with this, his current sales are ₹1,35,200, what was his sales (in ₹) two years ago?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

First year increase = 4% → Multiplying factor = 104/100 = 26/25

Second year increase = 25% → Multiplying factor = 125/100 = 5/4

Initial Sales × (26/25) × (5/4) = 1,35,200

Initial Sales = 1,35,200 × (25/26) × (4/5) = 5200 × 5 × 4 = 1,04,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,04,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f9c4f5e9246cf119c79aa87b9bd0035ecfca9c2ea8d90a20155b93497f06793.png] 

**Given:**

Current sales amount = **₹1,35,200**

First year growth = **4%**

Second year growth = **25%**

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sales two years ago be **x**.

⇒ x × (1 + 4/100) × (1 + 25/100) = 1,35,200

⇒ x × (104/100) × (125/100) = 1,35,200

⇒ x × (26/25) × (5/4) = 1,35,200

⇒ x × (130/100) = 1,35,200

⇒ x × 1.3 = 1,35,200

⇒ x = 1,35,200 / 1.3

⇒ x = 1,04,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,04,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

Effective Rate Calculation

In this case: 4 + 25 + (4 × 25)/100 = 29 + 1 = 30%. Thus, final value is 130% of the initial value.

Reverse Percentage

To find the initial value from the final value, divide the final value by the product of individual growth factors (1 + r/100).

130:
